title: One null nested record erases the nested records of every other element
rationale: The partial-loss sibling of the previous fixture and the more insidious one, because the array length survives so the result looks structurally plausible. A bare key emitted by the null element gives the field a value list, so the reconstructor takes the primitive branch instead of the record branch and the child node holding the real data is never read for any element.
catchesBugClass: Branch-selection shadowing: an incidental key emitted by one element diverting every element down the wrong reconstruction path. Distinct from the previous fixture precedence bug - a fix to one will not fix the other.
cannotCatch: Cannot catch the mirrored ordering where the null element comes first, which becomes a MISPLACEMENT rather than a deletion. It also cannot catch the analogous shadowing for a nullable nested ARRAY field, which fails by a different mechanism.

predicted.detail: The array length is right, the ids are right, and the nested record content is gone from every element. Silent, no exception, plausible-looking output.
